tag_paths: Successors and the freedom to revise

related_resources.reason: UNESCO documents construction begun 1248 and completed 1880, stages of work and the nineteenth-century fidelity to surviving medieval plans.
City tourism history reports a pause of more than three centuries, renewal in 1842 and completion in 1880.
The Broadbalk winter-wheat experiment began in autumn 1843, remains ongoing and includes long-running fertilizer and manure comparisons, including a no-fertilizer control.
Describes harvest records from 1844, archived grain and straw samples and alterations to harvesting methods and data series.
Long-term experimental layout, redivisions and comparisons involving rotations; context for methods that changed over time.
Notes continuing experiments after Lawes died and periodic management changes to remain scientifically relevant.
The Ise Jingu 20-year renewal ceremony, 2013 62nd ceremony, ritual and craft transmission over approximately 1300 years.
Details historical change and a long interruption in the renewal ceremony due to warfare; identifies restoration in the sixteenth century.
Documents 2033 plan for the next ceremony and public overview of Shikinen Sengu.
Reported ongoing 63rd renewal, its ritual meaning, material practices, craft transmission and historical interruptions; contextualizes costs.
Katie Paterson project begun 2014, planned 2114 publication, 1000 trees at Nordmarka, one author per year, trust and care of manuscripts.
Artist describes unread/unpublished manuscripts and specially designed room at Oslo public library; future publication is planned, not complete.
Museum records commissioning, institutional support, trust and conceptual structure of one-hundred-year artwork.

historical_claims.anchor: In Cologne, Germany, the cathedral began in the year twelve forty-eight and was not completed until eighteen eighty.
historical_claims.source_locator: UNESCO brief history; Cologne Tourism construction history

historical_claims.anchor: Work slowed, and eventually there was a pause lasting more than three centuries. Major construction resumed in the nineteenth century.
historical_claims.source_locator: Construction history: long pause between 16th and 19th centuries

historical_claims.anchor: The UNESCO account of the cathedral emphasizes the nineteenth-century builders' fidelity to the medieval plans.
At Rothamsted, an agricultural research center in England, researchers began an experiment in eighteen forty-three that continues today.
An unfertilized control has remained part of the design since the beginning.
historical_claims.source_locator: Original control treatment has never received fertilizer or manures since 1843

historical_claims.anchor: The field was divided into additional sections in nineteen sixty-eight to compare continuous wheat with rotations.
historical_claims.source_locator: Broadbalk overview, 1968 comparison of cropping/fallow and rotations

historical_claims.anchor: Harvesting and measurement methods have changed over time. Records and archived samples make it possible to ask which observations remain comparable, what changed, and why.
historical_claims.source_locator: Rothamsted changes from hand scythes through modern harvesting, yield data series and archives

historical_claims.anchor: At Ise Jingu, a Shinto shrine complex in Japan, the tradition known as Shikinen Sengu involves rebuilding principal sanctuary structures and renewing sacred objects on a roughly twenty-year cycle.
The tradition stretches back about thirteen hundred years, although it has not proceeded without historical interruptions.
historical_claims.source_locator: Kokugakuin university historical record, Sengukan museum

historical_claims.anchor: The sixty-second ceremony took place in twenty thirteen; the next cycle is directed toward twenty thirty-three.
In Oslo, artist Katie Paterson began a project in twenty fourteen called Future Library. It is intended to last until twenty one fourteen.
A thousand trees were planted in a forest outside the city. The plan is to use them to make paper for a collection of writing a century later.
Each year a writer contributes a text, and the manuscripts are held unpublished and unread until their eventual release. Margaret Atwood contributed the first text.
historical_claims.source_locator: Future Library annual writings and inaugural writer

historical_claims.anchor: The collection is kept under the care of a trust and associated with a specially designed room in Oslo's public library.
historical_claims.source_locator: Museum catalog and artist description of trust, room and institutional care

claim_evidence.anchor: The project had to become possible again after generations had learned to live with its incompleteness.
A design that outlives its designer is a triumph of transmission. A design that cannot be questioned has become something else.
claim_evidence.source_locator: UNESCO heritage history and design continuity
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Normative distinction between preserved design and binding authority.

claim_evidence.anchor: The field became useful in a second way: it made long time itself part of the experiment.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Analytic interpretation of why long-run continuity produces different evidence.

claim_evidence.anchor: A long experiment that hides changes to its methods may merely produce a long story. A long experiment that records those changes can produce evidence.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Rothamsted experiment layout and yield record histories
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Methodological argument about comparability and documented transitions.

claim_evidence.anchor: The shrine's Sengukan museum explains that periodic renewal is also a way of transmitting traditional techniques and cultural knowledge.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Museum explicitly says renewal transmits spirit and traditional techniques.

claim_evidence.anchor: A tradition survives not only by conserving objects but by repeatedly creating competent successors.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Essay synthesis; does not substitute secular framing for religious significance.

claim_evidence.anchor: Even the project itself has no guarantee of success. A forest is not a clock.
claim_evidence.source_locator: 2014–2114 project plan; no claim of completed outcome
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Normative observation of contingencies; not a prediction of failure.

claim_evidence.anchor: The future cannot sign that contract for us.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Future Library public trust and obligations
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Normative argument about consent of future caretakers.

claim_evidence.anchor: A bequest is not consent. We should say that clearly.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Ethical argument not proven by empirical case studies.

claim_evidence.anchor: If our idea of a successful inheritance requires them to admire us, we have left them a burden of gratitude rather than a useful piece of work.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Ethical argument about autonomy of successors
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent author argument informed by cases.

description: Considers how tools, records, and unfinished projects pass between generations of makers and why understandable handoffs make work reusable.
